newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai hanged in Singapore for taxi driver murder.
newsitem.headline: Thai hanged in Singapore for taxi driver murder.

text.p: A Thai worker was hanged in Singapore on Friday for murdering a taxi driver.
Pracha Thanomnin, 31, was allowed his last requests to watch a Thai kickboxing video and to eat sour prawn soup before going to the gallows, Thai state radio in Bangkok said.
Singapore's prison department confirmed a Thai had been hanged but declined to give further details of the case. The Thai embassy confirmed Pracha's identity but declined to give further comment.
The Thai embassy in Singapore provided Pracha with a videotape of recent kickboxing events but the convicted man's request for beer was not allowed, the radio station said.
The Bangkok Post newspaper said on Friday that Pracha, in a gesture of remorse for the murder, donated his organs to Singapore's General Hospital.
More than 280 people have been hanged in Singapore for various offences over the last 20 years. More than half of those hanged were convicted of drug trafficking.

Singapore's anti-drug laws include a mandatory death sentence for anyone over 18 years of age found guilty of trafficking more than 15 grams (half an ounce) of heroin, 30 grams (one ounce) of morphine or 500 grams (18 ounces) of cannabis.
